transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Avery Collins (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood CSM) -- Marcus Lee (Helix Procurement), Sofia Alvarez (Helix Legal), Jordan Price (Helix Cloud), Tanya Rhee (Helix Finance)

Auto-summary (auto): quick governance orientation, focused on MSA/DPA, SLA thresholds, pricing committee steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. I'm Avery, AE for Redwood Inference, with Priya our solutions engineer and Liam from CS. How's everyone doing?
[00:09] Marcus: Doing well, thanks. Busy month. We'll be quick, we have procurement committee at 2:30 PT tomorrow so trying to align things.
[00:16] Sofia: Hi, Sofia here from legal. I'll be driving MSA/DPA questions.
[00:19] Jordan: Jordan, infra. We'll want to understand the private deployment and KMS story.
[00:23] Priya: Great, quick agenda: MSA/DPA high level, SLA targets and credits, pricing approval path, then open for technical questions and next steps.
[00:31] Avery: One quick note, we put links in the calendar to our SOC 2 packet and the draft DPA — that's the working copy, not final.
[00:38] Marcus: Perfect. First question: on commercial terms, is there flexibility on commitment length vs unit price? Our CFO needs a 12-month view for budgeting.
[00:48] Avery: Yes, typical structure is usage-based for hosted, and reserved commits for Dedicated. We can do 12-month reserved pricing with tiered discounts. The pricing worksheet I'll share shows per-token unit economics at 0, 3, and 12 month commits. (slight cough) I'll include a worked example for Helix's projected throughput.
[01:08] Tanya (quiet): will that include overage handling?
[01:11] Avery: Yep, overage rules are in the worksheet and the MSA addendum. We can also include burst capacity terms if you care about spiky traffic.
[01:18] Sofia: On the DPA side, our main items are: data residency for EU customers, KMS/HSM controls, and audit log retention. Can you confirm encryption in transit+at rest and bring-your-own-key options?
[01:33] Priya: Yes, encryption in transit and at rest by default. For Private deployment and Dedicated we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations, and for on-prem we'll support HSM as part of the deployment plan. Note: in hosted there's also a BYOK path for dedicated tenants.
[01:48] Jordan: When you say BYOK, is that via AWS KMS exclusively or multi-cloud KMS? We run across GCP and Azure too.
[01:55] Priya: We support AWS KMS and a KMS abstraction layer; GCP KMS is supported, Azure can be supported in our private topology. I'll follow up with a tech note. (murmur)
[02:08] Marcus: SLA — we need 99.9% uptime, P95 latency under 350ms for inference in production for our low-latency pathways. Is that achievable in hosted?
[02:18] Priya: For our hosted API global endpoints, P95 under 350ms depends on model size and your prompt lengths. For smaller models it's typically sub-200ms. For P95 under 350 with larger LLMs we recommend Dedicated pools or the private deployment in region. We can also leverage prefix caching and batching to help.
[02:38] Jordan: What's the fallback plan if the region goes down? We need cross-region failover and an RTO of under 15 minutes.
[02:46] Avery: We have routing policies and automated fallbacks to compatible model variants in another region. For enterprise Dedicated we can configure active-passive failover; RTO depends on warm pools. We'll capture RTOs in the SLA appendix.
[02:58] Sofia: Credits calculation? We need an objective metric for downtime and latency SLO breaches.
[03:05] Priya: Credits are tiered: partial credits for degraded latency windows and higher credits for full downtime beyond defined grace periods. We'll include sample credit calculations in the SLA draft.
[03:16] Marcus: Procurement timeline question: our pricing committee meets weekly; what's a realistic timeframe to get to PO after MSA redlines?
[03:23] Avery: From acceptance of commercial terms and resolved DPA exceptions, typical procurement is 4-8 weeks, faster if we pre-align redlines and provide the standard MSA template early.
[03:32] Marcus: That velocity works for us if we get the MSA by Monday.
[03:35] Avery: We'll get the draft MSA with highlighted redlines by 2026-11-09.
[03:39] Jordan: For onboarding, can we pilot in our staging region for 2 weeks with a capped token budget? We want to validate latency and costs.
[03:47] Priya: Absolutely, we often run 2-week PoC pilots — we can spin up a dedicated pool mirror for staging and do a short benchmark. I'll run a baseline using a sample prompt set you share.
[03:58] Marcus: Who signs the MSA? Procurement or legal?
[04:02] Sofia: Legal needs to clear commercial and DPA redlines, procurement will manage PO.
[04:07] Avery: We'll mark stakeholders in the draft so it's clear who needs to sign.
[04:12] (pause)
[04:18] Sofia: A few DPA specifics — can you preserve row-level deletion for customer PII and provide proof of deletion? We have some EU regs.
[04:27] Priya: We maintain data deletion controls, and for private deployments we can guarantee retention windows matching your policy. For hosted, we can contractually commit to deletion and provide audit logs; we'll need to scope the exact retention and deletion evidence in the DPA appendix.
[04:42] Maria (automated note): Speaker mislabeling sometimes; apologies.
[04:45] Jordan: Any limits on KV cache persistence? We're worried about long-lived KV caches holding sensitive context.
[04:53] Priya: KV cache is ephemeral by default; for caching between requests we can define TTLs and optionally disable persistence. We'll document defaults and override controls.
[05:04] Marcus: Pricing approval — our CFO wants to see the unit economics and break-even point. Can you show a 12-month TCO model?
[05:12] Avery: Yes, we'll include a 12-month TCO scenario and a sensitivity analysis for token volumes. I'll also show delta between hosted and dedicated.
[05:21] Tanya: On invoicing, do you offer net-30 or net-60?
[05:24] Avery: Standard is net-30, net-60 can be considered at enterprise contract stage. We'll flag that as a negotiable term.
[05:31] Sofia: On indemnities — we may need narrower IP indemnity carveouts for generated content. Is that standard?
[05:39] Avery: We can review indemnity language; this comes up often. We'll propose standard language plus an optional addendum for generative output carveouts.
[05:48] Priya: Technical note — if you need sub-200ms P95 for heavy models, the combination of Dedicated pools with quantized model variants and colocated infra will be the path. There's a tradeoff with cost.
[06:00] Jordan: Understood. We'll want the benchmark numbers.
[06:03] Priya: I'll run a 1-hour test simulating your average payloads — that'll give us P95 and cost per 1k tokens estimate.
[06:11] Marcus: On security artifacts, we need SOC2 Type II report and ISO27001 certificate. Is that public?
[06:17] Liam: We can provide redacted artifacts and an NDA-protected bundle for in-depth review. I'll share the link and the contact for security questionnaire responses.
[06:27] Sofia: Also: any customers in our industry references? Financial services references help accelerate risk acceptance.
[06:33] Avery: We can share customer references in finance and a short case study. I'll include that in the packet.
[06:39] Marcus: One more — do you do data residency per tenant in EU region? We need EU-citizen data to remain in EU clusters.
[06:47] Priya: For Dedicated and Private we can pin tenants to region clusters; for hosted we offer EU-only hosting regions and contractual commitments. We'll include region residency clause examples.
[06:58] Sofia: About audit logs: we need 12 months of logs, SSO with SAML and RBAC.
[07:04] Priya: SAML SSO and RBAC are supported. Log retention we can extend per plan; 12 months is typical for enterprise.
[07:11] Marcus: Any blockers from Redwood side for contract execution?
[07:15] Avery: No blockers; main items are DPA exception list from you and the procurement PO signoff. If we align quickly on redlines we can hit your procurement window.
[07:24] Jordan: For the pilot, will you require any specific access patterns or IP whitelisting?
[07:30] Priya: We'll need IP ranges and a service account for the pilot. For private deployment we'd work through network diagrams.
[07:36] Sofia: Can you confirm the data processing addendum supports subprocessor disclosure?
[07:42] Liam: Yes, DPA includes subprocessor list and we keep it updated. We'll share the current list and the on-request process for notifying new subs.
[07:51] (brief hold while Avery pulls a doc)
[08:00] Avery: Ok, quick recap and next steps from Redwood side: share draft MSA with pricing worksheet by 2026-11-09, SOC2/ISO artifacts and security contact by 2026-11-06, Priya will run a short performance run and post results by 2026-11-10. You'll share DPA exceptions and residency constraints by 2026-11-12.
[08:18] Marcus: That sounds good. If we get the MSA by Monday, the procurement committee can review next week.
[08:24] Sofia: We'll try to consolidate redlines and get them over by 2026-11-12.
[08:29] Avery: Great, we'll then schedule a security deep-dive with your infra/security folks for week of 2026-11-16.
[08:35] Tanya: Finance will review TCO and likely ask for net-60 but we can discuss.
[08:39] Avery: Noted. Anything else before we wrap?
[08:44] Jordan: No, that's it from infra. Thanks.
[08:47] Sofia: Thanks everyone.
[08:49] Avery: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the packet.
[08:53] (meeting ends)

Notes: occasional ASR mislabels (Maria note) — some product names like Redwood Dedicated were transcribed as 'Redwood Dedicatd' in the raw file. Links referenced: [MSA draft link], [SOC2 packet link], [Performance worksheet link].
